nodes.question: How does the court rule on the damages motion: the verdict stands, the court remits to the most the evidence supports, or the court orders a new trial on damages?
nodes.label: Damages: stands / remit / new trial

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a)(1)(A): after a jury trial the court may grant a new trial on all or some of the issues "for any reason for which a new trial has heretofore been granted in an action at law in federal court." A new trial may be granted even where the evidence is legally sufficient to support the verdict, when the verdict is contrary to the great weight of the evidence, so that a new trial is necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice (Roebuck v. Drexel Univ., 852 F.2d 715, 735-36 (3d Cir. 1988)). "[N]ew trials because the verdict is against the weight of the evidence are proper only when the record shows that the jury's verdict resulted in a miscarriage of justice or where the verdict, on the record, cries out to be overturned or shocks our conscience" (Williamson v. Consolidated Rail Corp., 926 F.2d 1344, 1353 (3d Cir. 1991)). An award "so grossly excessive as to shock the judicial conscience" is set aside: the court remits it to the maximum recovery that does not shock the judicial conscience, or orders a new trial (Gumbs v. Pueblo Int'l, Inc., 823 F.2d 768, 771-74 (3d Cir. 1987)).

Remittitur is to the maximum the evidence supports, and the plaintiff may refuse it and take a new trial (Hetzel v. Prince William County, 523 U.S. 208 (1998); Kazan v. Wolinski, 721 F.2d 911 (3d Cir. 1983)).

nodes.question: Does the court set aside the patent verdict?
nodes.label: Patent verdict set aside

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b); JMOL only where the record lacks the minimum evidence to support the verdict (Lightning Lube v. Witco, 4 F.3d 1153, 1166 (3d Cir. 1993)).

Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a)(1)(A): after a jury trial the court may grant a new trial on all or some of the issues "for any reason for which a new trial has heretofore been granted in an action at law in federal court." A new trial may be granted even where the evidence is legally sufficient to support the verdict, when the verdict is contrary to the great weight of the evidence, so that a new trial is necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice (Roebuck v. Drexel Univ., 852 F.2d 715, 735-36 (3d Cir. 1988)). "[N]ew trials because the verdict is against the weight of the evidence are proper only when the record shows that the jury's verdict resulted in a miscarriage of justice or where the verdict, on the record, cries out to be overturned or shocks our conscience" (Williamson v. Consolidated Rail Corp., 926 F.2d 1344, 1353 (3d Cir. 1991)). An award "so grossly excessive as to shock the judicial conscience" is set aside: the court remits it to the maximum recovery that does not shock the judicial conscience, or orders a new trial (Gumbs v. Pueblo Int'l, Inc., 823 F.2d 768, 771-74 (3d Cir. 1987)).

nodes.question: Does the court grant the motion to treble under the unfair-trade-practices statute?
nodes.label: Trebling

steps.text: N.C. Gen. Stat. §75-16: once a violation of §75-1.1 is found, "judgment shall be rendered ... for treble the amount fixed by the verdict." The plaintiff elects between the trebled and the punitive recovery and takes the larger (United Labs. v. Kuykendall, 335 N.C. 183 (1993)).

Trebling a trade-secret award after the jury answered 'No' to the unfair-trade-practices question: the authorities each side relies on. Against trebling: this court's order of 14 May 2024 on the defendants' Rule 50(a) motion (D.I. 590) held that North Carolina courts have "not recognized head start benefits to the Defendants as such a proxy" for the plaintiff's injury and that "[t]he jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury"; §75-16 trebles damages, and a restitutionary award is not trebled (Winant v. Bostic, 5 F.3d 767, 775-76 (4th Cir. 1993)); a violation of the Trade Secrets Protection Act is not in itself a violation of §75-1.1 (Drouillard v. Keister Williams Newspaper Servs., 108 N.C. App. 169 (1992); Legacy Data Access, LLC v. MediQuant, Inc. (W.D.N.C. 2017), which declined to treble a trade-secret verdict where the jury awarded $1 on the unfair-trade-practices claim); and Qorvo filed no Rule 50 motion, the route for setting aside a jury finding for want of evidence (Unitherm Food Sys., Inc. v. Swift-Eckrich, Inc., 546 U.S. 394 (2006)). For trebling: the jury finds the facts, and the court decides as a matter of law whether they amount to an unfair or deceptive practice (Hardy v. Toler, 288 N.C. 303 (1975)); "A violation of the Trade Secrets Protection Act constitutes an unfair act or practice under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-1.1" (Medical Staffing Network, Inc. v. Ridgway, 194 N.C. App. 649 (2009)); and Grout Doctor Global Franchise Corp. v. Groutman, Inc. (E.D.N.C. 2015), which Qorvo cites (D.I. 587).

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

File: a petition on the decision date + 0 days; on a levy day, the company's payment or petition comes before the levy
Neither: the company takes no further step on the judgment; a later petition comes from the notes or the cash floor
A filing: collections stop on the petition date (11 U.S.C. §362(a)); the outstanding balance is a stayed claim
On the loan: from the petition Slope collects nothing and funds no draw; the balance owed is frozen, and collections in the 90 days before it are clawback exposure
How does the judgment debtor respond to an enforceable, unstayed, unpaid judgment: pay, seek a sale or financing, file for bankruptcy, or neither?

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

Pay: pays the amount owed with interest on the decision date; an option where the company's cash covers the amount on some trajectory
Seek sale or financing: moves the decision to file to the next decision date; books no cash
File: a petition on the decision date + 0 days; on a levy day, the company's payment or petition comes before the levy
Neither: the company takes no further step on the judgment; a later petition comes from the notes or the cash floor

On the loan: from the petition Slope collects nothing and funds no draw; the balance owed is frozen, and collections in the 90 days before it are clawback exposure

we effectively have 3.0 million available unissued and unreserved authorized shares to meet the needs of our business.

Absent an increase in the shares of common stock authorized for issuance under our Certificate of Incorporation, we will be limited to non-equity financing structures in the event additional financing is required.
Additionally, the terms of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 impose certain limitations on our ability to incur additional debt obligations.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.

we believe there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
we effectively have 3.0 million available unissued and unreserved authorized shares to meet the needs of our business.

Additionally, the terms of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 impose certain limitations on our ability to incur additional debt obligations.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.

we believe there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
we effectively have 3.0 million available unissued and unreserved authorized shares to meet the needs of our business.

Absent an increase in the shares of common stock authorized for issuance under our Certificate of Incorporation, we will be limited to non-equity financing structures in the event additional financing is required.
Additionally, the terms of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 impose certain limitations on our ability to incur additional debt obligations.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.
